arxiv-1807-09846.title: Diffusion and consensus on weakly connected directed graphs
arxiv-1807-09846.creator: J. J. P. Veerman, E. Kummel
arxiv-1807-09846.description: Abstract Let G G be a weakly connected directed graph with asymmetric graph Laplacian ℒ {\cal L} . Consensus and diffusion are dual dynamical processes defined on G G by x ˙ = − ℒ ​ x \dot{x}=-{\cal L}x for consensus and p ˙ = − p ​ ℒ \dot{p}=-p{\cal L} for diffusion.

arxiv-1903-02778.title: The multiple symmetry sustaining phase transitions of spin ice
arxiv-1903-02778.creator: V. Raban, C. T. Suen, L. Berthier, P. C. W. Holdsworth
arxiv-1903-02778.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by V. Raban, C. T. Suen, L. Berthier, P. C. W. Holdsworth. We present the full phase diagram of the dumbbell model of spin ice as a function of temperature, chemical potential and staggered chemical potential which breaks the translational lattice symmetry in favour of charge crystal ordering. We observe a double winged structure with five possible phases, monopole fluid (spin ice), fragmented single monopole crystal phases and double monopole crystal, the zinc blend structure.

arxiv-2212-00747.title: Quasi Normal Modes of Black Holes and Detection in Ringdown Process
arxiv-2212-00747.creator: Yuqian Zhao 1,2 , Bing Sun 3 , Zhan-Feng Mai 4 and Zhoujian Cao 1,2,∗
arxiv-2212-00747.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuqian Zhao 1,2 , Bing Sun 3 , Zhan-Feng Mai 4 and Zhoujian Cao 1,2,∗. Quasi-normal modes (QNMs) of a black hole (BH) are the eigen modes describing the dissipative oscillation of various fields in that spacetime, which can be intrinsically produced by the linear perturbation theory.

arxiv-2312-06199.title: Towards Transferable Adversarial Attacks with Centralized Perturbation
arxiv-2312-06199.creator: Shangbo Wu, Yu-an Tan, Yajie Wang, Ruinan Ma, Wencong Ma, Yuanzhang Li
arxiv-2312-06199.description: Abstract Adversarial transferability enables black-box attacks on unknown victim deep neural networks (DNNs), rendering attacks viable in real-world scenarios. Current transferable attacks create adversarial perturbation over the entire image, resulting in excessive noise that overfit the source model. Concentrating perturbation to dominant image regions that are model-agnostic is crucial to improving adversarial efficacy.

arxiv-2403-15767.title: The sharp C 0 C^{0} -fragmentation property for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms and homeomorphisms on surfaces
arxiv-2403-15767.creator: Baptiste Serraille
arxiv-2403-15767.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Baptiste Serraille. In this paper, we present a C 0 C^{0} -fragmentation property for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. More precisely, it is known that for a given open covering 𝒰 \mathcal{U} of a compact symplectic surface we can write each C 0 C^{0} -small enough Hamiltonian diffeomorphism as the composition of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms compactly supported inside the open sets of the covering 𝒰 \mathcal{U} .

arxiv-2409-11835.description: Abstract In recent years, speech diffusion models have advanced rapidly. Alongside the widely used U-Net architecture, transformer-based models such as the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) have also gained attention. However, current DiT speech models treat Mel spectrograms as general images, which overlooks the specific acoustic properties of speech.

pmc-10604302.title: On the Use of Machine Learning Techniques and Non-Invasive Indicators for Classifying and Predicting Cardiac Disorders
pmc-10604302.creator: Raydonal Ospina, Adenice G O Ferreira, Hélio M de Oliveira, Víctor Leiva, Cecilia Castro, Dimitrios A Vrachatis, Spyridon G Deftereos, Theodore G Papaioannou
pmc-10604302.description: This research aims to enhance the classification and prediction of ischemic heart diseases using machine learning techniques, with a focus on resource efficiency and clinical applicability. Specifically, we introduce novel non-invasive indicators known as Campello de Souza features, which require only a tensiometer and a clock for data collection.

pmc-10663099.title: Microbial Profile of Fresh and Semicooked Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) and Hygienic Practice of Fish Handlers in Hawassa, Ethiopia
pmc-10663099.creator: Fasika Admasu, Abraham Mikru, Kassaye Balkew, Million Adane
pmc-10663099.description: Despite its high nutritional quality, fish is a highly perishable food item. This study aimed at assessing the microbial quality and safety of fresh and semicooked Nile tilapia fish fillets and the food safety practices of fish handlers in Hawassa City.

pmc-11434759.title: Efficacy and Safety of the Combination of Palmitoylethanolamide, Superoxide Dismutase, Alpha Lipoic Acid, Vitamins B12, B1, B6, E, Mg, Zn and Nicotinamide for 6 Months in People with Diabetic Neuropathy
pmc-11434759.creator: Triantafyllos Didangelos, Eleni Karlafti, Evangelia Kotzakioulafi, Parthena Giannoulaki, Zisis Kontoninas, Anastasia Kontana, Polykarpos Evripidou, Christos Savopoulos, Andreas L. Birkenfeld, Konstantinos Kantartzis

pmc-12535730.title: Validation and Comparison of BAP-65, DECAF, NEWS, and a Novel Combined Score for Predicting in-Hospital Mortality in Patients with Acute Exacerbation of COPD
pmc-12535730.creator: Maria Boesing, Giorgia Lüthi-Corridori, Laurin Manuel Sarbach, Fabienne Jaun, Daniel Olejar, Michael Brändle, Jörg D Leuppi
pmc-12535730.description: PurposeAcute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are a major cause of hospital admissions and are associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Several scoring systems are available for early risk stratification, such as DECAF, BAP-65, and NEWS, each incorporating parameters from different clinical domains.

pmc-12598173.title: “Pinch-and-Tuck” Arthroscopic Technique for Capsular Laxity in Posterior Shoulder Instability
pmc-12598173.creator: Chirag D Sheth, Larry D Field
pmc-12598173.description: Shoulder instability is a common orthopaedic condition that often requires surgical intervention. Anterior instability occurs more commonly, but posterior instability is increasingly recognized and managed as well. Trends toward earlier surgical intervention for instability patients have been recently promoted, and surgical management is continually evolving as more data and new techniques are published.

pmc-12839438.title: Autogenous Tooth Bone Grafts with Enamel Matrix Derivates in Non-Contained Intrabony Periodontal Defects—A Case Series Study
pmc-12839438.creator: Eleonora Solyom, Kristóf Forgó, Kristof Somodi, Daniel Palkovics, Szilard Vancsa, Peter Windisch, Balint Molnar, Reka Fazekas
pmc-12839438.description: Background: The predictability of regenerative outcomes in non-contained intrabony periodontal defects remains limited. Autogenous tooth bone grafts (ATB) may represent a biologically active and osteoconductive scaffold with minimal residual graft material. This study evaluated the clinical and radiographic outcomes of ATB combined with enamel matrix derivative (EMD) in intrabony defects.

pmc-13478490.creator: Thomas J Baumgarten, Lua Koenig, Richard Hardstone, Adeen Flinker, Sasha Devore, Daniel Friedman, Patricia Dugan, Orrin Devinsky, Biyu J He
pmc-13478490.description: Prediction of future events is essential for guiding effective actions in dynamic environments. Studies on the neural mechanisms for time-forward predictions have typically used stimuli with relatively simple statistical regularities. Here, we investigated time-forward predictions using stimuli containing statistical regularities similar to those found in natural auditory stimuli.

pmc-13607304.creator: Ahmet Burak Keçeci, Emrah Yeşil
pmc-13607304.description: Background: Radial artery spasm (RAS) is a major complication of transradial coronary angiography (TRA) that adversely affects procedural success and patient comfort.
